title: AffineHeavyTailedAdam.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable optimization on R^d, permitting nonconvex objectives. The initial objective gap satisfies f(x0) − inf_x f(x) ≤ Δ, with Δ ≥ 0; attainment of the infimum is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineHeavyTailedAdam.lean: spec.Instance, spec.admissible gradient and initial-gap conditions, spec.valid.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call returns a full vector g(x, ξ) using a fresh IID sample. The oracle is unbiased: E[g(x, ξ)] = ∇f(x). Coordinates within a sample need not be independent. Oracle cost counts individual samples, including every sample in a minibatch.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: For L1‖y−x‖∞ ≤ 1, ‖∇f(y)−∇f(x)‖1 ≤ (L0 + L1‖∇f(x)‖1)‖y−x‖∞. Here L0,L1 ≥ 0 and L0+L1 > 0; either coefficient may vanish.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineHeavyTailedAdam.lean: sumNorm, maxNorm, spec.valid, spec.admissible smoothness condition.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x and coordinate i, E[|g_i(x,ξ)−∇_i f(x)|^p] ≤ σ0(i)^p + σ1^p|∇_i f(x)|^p, where 1 < p ≤ 2 and σ0(i),σ1 ≥ 0. This is a coordinatewise affine central-moment condition; finite variance is not required when p < 2.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineHeavyTailedAdam.lean: spec.valid and spec.admissible coordinatewise moment conditions.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: Smoothness pairs ℓ∞ displacement with ℓ1 gradient variation; stationarity is measured in ℓ1, although points are represented in Euclidean space.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is R^d for a public natural-number dimension d.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All setup parameters are public, including L0, L1, σ0, σ1, p, Δ, ε and x0; the objective and sampling law are hidden. Allowed algorithms use the supplied minibatched, bias-corrected Adam family with fixed configuration, β1,β2 ∈ [0,1), positive stepsize and denominator offset, and positive batch size.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/AffineHeavyTailedAdam.lean: Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, Config, coreStep, spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The output X must satisfy E[‖∇f(X)‖1] ≤ ε, with ε > 0. The norm is unsquared. The output must be measurable and its gradient ℓ1 norm integrable. The allowed method saves an iterate selected uniformly by its initialization seed.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee averages over both the algorithm's random seed and the IID oracle sequence, under their product probability law, with a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines coordinatewise gradient-dependent heavy-tailed noise, local ℓ∞-to-ℓ1 generalized smoothness, and expected ℓ1 stationarity within a restricted Adam family. These are meaningful departures from the classical globally smooth, bounded-variance benchmark.

descriptionHtml:
Adam with Affine Heavy-Tailed Noise

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R, where d≥0 is an integer. The function f is (L0,L1)-smooth in the ℓ∞-to-ℓ1 sense, with L0,L1≥0 and L0+L1>0. A given starting point x0 satisfies f(x0)−infxf(x)≤Δ, where Δ≥0. The oracle returns unbiased stochastic gradients from independent, identically distributed samples, with coordinatewise noise moments of order p∈(1,2] bounded affinely in the corresponding gradient magnitudes to power p. We analyze minibatch Adam with bias correction. For ε>0, its output x¯ must satisfy E∥∇f(x¯)∥1≤ε, where expectation includes sampling and algorithm randomness and ∥z∥1=∑i=1d|zi|.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). The ambient space has its Euclidean inner product, which defines ∇f. Write ∥z∥∞=max1≤i≤d|zi|, with both norms equal to zero when d=0. Let Ω be a measurable sample space, and let σ0=(σ0,i)i=1d and σ1 be nonnegative noise parameters. The algorithm receives d, Ω, L0, L1, σ0, σ1, p, Δ, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Generalized smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere. For all x,y∈Rd satisfying L1∥y−x∥∞≤1, ∥∇f(y)−∇f(x)∥1≤(L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥1)∥y−x∥∞.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective gap). The given starting point satisfies f(x0)−f(x)≤Δfor every x∈Rd.

Assumption 3 (Affine heavy-tailed oracle). There exist a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:Rd×Ω→Rd. For every x, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x). For every x and coordinate i, the random variable |gi(x,ξ)−∇if(x)|p is integrable and satisfies Eξ∼ν[|gi(x,ξ)−∇if(x)|p]≤σ0,ip+σ1p|∇if(x)|p. At call k≥0, a query x∈Rd receives g(x,ξk). Under their joint law Q, the measurable samples (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent and each has distribution ν. Algorithm randomness is independent of this sample sequence.

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze minibatch Adam with bias correction and a constant step size. Its tuning parameters satisfy 0≤β1<1,0≤β2<1,η>0,δ>0,B∈{1,2,…},n∈{0,1,…}. These parameters may depend on the supplied inputs. Initialize the moments at m0=v0=0 and the iterate at the given x0. At iteration t≥0, take B consecutive oracle samples at xt and form ht=1B∑b=0B−1g(xt,ξtB+b). For each coordinate i, the update is mt+1=β1mt+(1−β1)ht,vit+1=β2vit+(1−β2)(hit)2,m^t+1=mt+11−β1t+1,v^t+1=vt+11−β2t+1,xit+1=xit−ηm^it+1v^it+1+δ. Each completed iteration uses B oracle calls. For an allotted budget N∈{0,1,…}, let T=⌊N/B⌋ be the number of completed iterations. Any remaining calls are made at xT and do not produce another update.

Independently of the samples, draw J uniformly from {0,…,n}. The output rule saves the selected iterate immediately before its update; explicitly, x¯={xJ,J<T,x0,J≥T. In particular, when N≥B(n+1), this is a uniform selection from x0,…,xn. Let P be the joint law of J and the oracle samples. The output must be measurable, ∥∇f(x¯)∥1 must be integrable under P, and the required accuracy is EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥1]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
Differentiable f:Rd→R satisfies f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ for every x and ∥∇f(y)−∇f(x)∥1≤(L0+L1∥∇f(x)∥1)∥y−x∥∞ whenever L1∥y−x∥∞≤1. Here L0,L1,Δ,σ0,i,σ1≥0, L0+L1>0, 1<p≤2, and ε>0. IID samples have law μ; the jointly measurable oracle is integrable, with ∫g(x,ω)dμ=∇f(x) and integrable coordinate errors satisfying ∫|gi(x,ω)−∂if(x)|pdμ≤σ0,ip+σ1p|∂if(x)|p. The setup restricts algorithms to bias-corrected coordinatewise Adam with arithmetic minibatches and a uniformly selected pre-update iterate xI. The target is ∫∥∇f(xI)∥1dP≤ε, with measurable output and integrable gradient norm; P includes the IID samples and independent uniform selection.

(1): Matches known rate for fixed p using canonical bias-corrected Adam with fixed memories (0.9,0.999); no problem-class complexity improvement. (1) has much larger constants, including 217q, unbounded as p↓1.
(3) Minibatch signSGD (Kornilov et al. 2025), Thm. 1 O([1+ΔdL0Eε2+Δd3/2L1Eε]
⋅[1+(s0/ε)q](1+log⁡(1/α))) calls for average gradient norm ≤ε with probability 1−α; Euclidean generalized smoothness, σ1=0.		 (1): Scope extends to affine noise and anchored ℓ∞→ℓ1 smoothness; (2) already covers this problem class. No established same-guarantee rate improvement. (1) gives expected accuracy, not the high-probability average-gradient guarantee of (3).
(4) Adam (Li et al. 2026), Cor. 1 O(1+dLΔε2+d2LΔσ2ε4) single-sample calls; p=2, L1=σ1=0, Euclidean L-smoothness and variance σ2. (1): Extends Adam to p<2, affine noise and generalized smoothness; fixed memories. On the overlap, no worse order if L0≤dL, s0≤dσ, dLΔ≥ε2. For L0=L, s0=σ, LΔ≥ε2, σ≥ε: O(LΔσ2/ε4) versus O(d2LΔσ2/ε4). (1) needs batches of order 1+s02/ε2, accuracy-dependent damping and a much smaller step. If dLΔ<ε2, its additional s02/ε2 cost can be worse.
(5) Vector Adam (Pang 2026), Thm. 6.4 Polynomial cost for relaxed (ρ,ε)-stationarity; bounded gradients, additive p-moment noise, p>4/3. Different criterion and function class; rates not comparable. (1): Ordinary gradient stationarity, unbounded gradients and all 1<p≤2 under generalized smoothness; canonical updates instead of random step multipliers. (1) requires generalized smoothness and accuracy-sized batches; (5) does not require gradient Lipschitz regularity.

L0E,L1E are Euclidean generalized-smoothness constants; L is the Euclidean gradient Lipschitz constant; σ2 bounds E∥g−∇f∥22 in (4). ρ>0 is the relaxation parameter in (5). The O constants in (2), (3) may depend on fixed p; all costs count individual stochastic-gradient calls, including batches.

source:
import LongTails.Setups.HeavyTailedAdam

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.AffineHeavyTailedAdam

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Point (d : ℕ) := Adam.Point d

noncomputable def sumNorm {d : ℕ} (x : Point d) : ℝ := ∑ i, |x i|

noncomputable def maxNorm {d : ℕ} (x : Point d) : ℝ := ‖WithLp.ofLp x‖

structure Config where
  β₁ : ℝ
  β₂ : ℝ
  η : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  batchSize : ℕ
  lastIndex : ℕ

structure State (d : ℕ) where
  count : ℕ
  total : Point d
  core : Adam.State d

noncomputable def coreStep {d : ℕ} (cfg : Config) (s : Adam.State d)
    (g : Point d) : Adam.State d :=
  let m := cfg.β₁ • s.momentum + (1 - cfg.β₁) • g
  let v := Adam.secondMomentStep (1 - cfg.β₂) s.secondMoment g
  let mhat := (1 - cfg.β₁ ^ (s.time + 1))⁻¹ • m
  let vhat := (1 - cfg.β₂ ^ (s.time + 1))⁻¹ • v
  { selected := s.selected
    time := s.time + 1
    point := s.point - cfg.η • Adam.direction cfg.δ mhat vhat
    momentum := m
    secondMoment := v
    saved := if s.time = s.selected then s.point else s.saved }

noncomputable def step {d : ℕ} (cfg : Config) (s : State d) (g : Point d) : State d :=
  if s.count + 1 < cfg.batchSize then
    { count := s.count + 1, total := s.total + g, core := s.core }
  else
    { count := 0, total := 0
      core := coreStep cfg s.core ((cfg.batchSize : ℝ)⁻¹ • (s.total + g)) }

noncomputable def method {d : ℕ} (cfg : Config) (x0 : Point d) :
    Algorithm (Point d) (Point d) (Point d) where
  Seed := Fin (cfg.lastIndex + 1)
  law := ⟨(PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (cfg.lastIndex + 1))).toMeasure, inferInstance⟩
  State := State d
  initial k := ⟨0, 0, ⟨k.val, 0, x0, 0, 0, x0⟩⟩
  query s := (0, s.core.point)
  update := step cfg
  output s := s.core.saved

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L0 : ℝ
  L1 : ℝ
  σ0 : Fin d → ℝ
  σ1 : ℝ
  p : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : Point d

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := Point q.d → ℝ
  Query q := Point q.d
  Reply q := Point q.d
  Output q := Point q.d
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 ≤ q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 < q.L0 + q.L1 ∧
    (∀ i, 0 ≤ q.σ0 i) ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ1 ∧ 1 < q.p ∧ q.p ≤ 2 ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : Point q.d → q.Ω → Point q.d)
      (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, x) ω => g x ω } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, q.L1 * maxNorm (y - x) ≤ 1 →
        sumNorm (gradient f y - gradient f x) ≤
          (q.L0 + q.L1 * sumNorm (gradient f x)) * maxNorm (y - x)) ∧
      (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, Integrable (g x) p) ∧
      (∀ x, ∫ ω, g x ω ∂p = gradient f x) ∧
      (∀ x i, Integrable (fun ω => |(g x ω - gradient f x) i| ^ q.p) p) ∧
      (∀ x i, ∫ ω, |(g x ω - gradient f x) i| ^ q.p ∂p ≤
        q.σ0 i ^ q.p + q.σ1 ^ q.p * |gradient f x i| ^ q.p)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => sumNorm (gradient f (output ω))) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, sumNorm (gradient f (output ω)) ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm q A :=
    ∃ cfg : Config, 0 ≤ cfg.β₁ ∧ cfg.β₁ < 1 ∧ 0 ≤ cfg.β₂ ∧ cfg.β₂ < 1 ∧
      0 < cfg.η ∧ 0 < cfg.δ ∧ 0 < cfg.batchSize ∧ A = method cfg q.x0

end LongTails.Setups.AffineHeavyTailedAdam
